Alaska.Ai — The Stack Draft

2026-08-21 · branch claude/linkedin-stack-2026-08-21

Copy this for LinkedIn

A Delaware LLC formed in January has filed to bank a stretch of Cook Inlet seabed off Nikiski for an underwater AI data center. No Alaska party is legally able to object to it yet.

DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC proposed a 100-megawatt tidal data center with up to 350 underwater turbines and 66 “hives” housing AI servers, per Anchorage Daily News, 19 August. ADN describes only an application “to conduct preliminary environmental and engineering studies.” Read against 16 U.S.C. 798, that filing is a preliminary permit.

It authorizes no construction and no entry onto waters owned by others. Its only legal effect is to freeze first-in-time priority to file a license application over a defined corridor, four years, extendable four more.

Five layers, in order.

- Corridor claim, 18 CFR 4.81 fixes the description, study plan and boundary maps, filed by the applicant.
- Acceptance gate, 18 CFR 4.32(e) judges whether the filing conforms, controlled by the Director, FERC Office of Energy Projects.
- The asset, priority in time and nothing else, set by Congress at 16 U.S.C. 798.
- Public notice, which opens the intervention and competing-application window, issued by FERC Secretary Kimberly D. Bose.
- Contested or uncontested fork, 18 CFR 375.308 delegated final action, back to that same Director.

Layer 2 is the chokepoint. FERC’s Northwest Branch sent DeepGreen a deficiency letter on 18 June 2026. The cure window is capped at 45 days, and a failed cure means any resubmission carries a new filing date, sending the priority claim to the back of the queue. Conformance preserves the original date and triggers the notice. FERC spokesperson Celeste Miller told ADN the application is still under review. The call is live. Not a hearing, not a vote. A letter.

This is site-banking, not power development. A 100 MW behind-the-meter buyer would solve the offtake problem that has killed every prior Cook Inlet tidal proposal, which is why the corridor is worth optioning. The cost to Alaska is standing. AEA, whose CEO Curtis Thayer told ADN the authority had never heard of DeepGreen, plus Homer Electric at Bernice Lake, the Kenai Peninsula Borough and area tribes, can’t intervene or file a competing application until FERC accepts.

FERC noticed a permit in this same corridor before, to Littoral Power Systems at P-15317-000, prescribing 60 days from issuance. Last week’s Bradley Lake anatomy shared that delegation rule, but that was an amendment to an existing license decided on the merits. Here the gate decides a filing date before anyone can be heard.

Draft the intervention now and set an eLibrary alert on Cook Inlet hydrokinetic filings. The clock runs from notice issuance, not from discovery.

Should Alaska utilities and boroughs file defensive preliminary permits on corridors they’ll need, instead of contesting someone else’s claim after that letter goes out?

#AlaskaAI #EnergyPolicy #DataCenters #GridPolicy

SHIPPED. Scorer 8.83 / 10 weighted against config/stack_rubric.yaml (threshold 8.0), all seven hard-fail checks passed. Editor shipped on cycle 2. Artwork scored 8.565 weighted against the artwork skill's rubric (floor 8.5) after six eval iterations, qa_check PASS.

MECHANISM. The FERC preliminary permit as a site-banking instrument, and the 18 CFR 4.32(e) deficiency-and-acceptance gate that manufactures the priority date. Triggered by ADN's 19 August report that Delaware-based DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC has filed over a roughly 1,650-acre Cook Inlet corridor off Nikiski for a 100 MW underwater AI data center.

WHY THIS ONE. Four scouts returned nine candidates. The accuracy gate cleared exactly one and killed the rest. Two deserve flagging because they were strong:
1. USACE North Slope permit RGP-05, reissued unchanged 17 August through 2031. Best document trail of the entire sweep, every layer re-verified from the binary PDFs including the signature and the embedded ADEC 401 certificate. DROPPED for failing the AI-tie test. The 32-page instrument never mentions compute or data centers, no compute applicant has filed a verification request, and its quantified consequence rested on acreage figures sourced to an advocacy group that could not be replaced with primary documentation. Running it would have meant an AI column about a gravel-fill permit on an inferred connection. It becomes an immediate pick the moment a compute applicant actually files.
2. UAF's 499 million dollar sole-source UARC IDIQ (W911NF-26-D-A013), awarded 7 August. Excellent mechanism, unusual chokepoint (a ceiling that obligates zero dollars). DROPPED because none of six fetched primary sources contains the words "artificial intelligence" or "machine learning" and the chokepoint was spread across two actors.

ACCURACY WORK WORTH KNOWING ABOUT. The gate caught and corrected four defects rather than inheriting them. The regulatory scout misquoted the ADN trigger twice; corrected against the live page. The scout's claim that "18 CFR 4.36 gives a 60-day window" is a misreading, 4.36 ties competing filings to the deadline prescribed in the public notice, and the post is phrased accordingly. The chokepoint actor was re-identified as the Director, Office of Energy Projects, whom 4.32(e) names directly, which removed an unverifiable branch-chief name from the piece entirely. A sixth layer on Cook Inlet beluga critical habitat was DROPPED because corridor containment could not be verified. Separately, two scouts returned irreconcilable 8(a) thresholds; FAR 19.808-1 says 30 million dollars with no defense/civilian split, which falsified a contractor page claiming 25M/100M and killed that candidate's layer.

NOT ASSERTED IN THE POST, all deliberately. No FERC docket number for DeepGreen (eLibrary was unfetchable on four attempts; P-15317-000 belongs to Littoral Power Systems and is attributed to them only). No name for the official who signed the 18 June deficiency letter. No claim that FERC has accepted or rejected; status is pending per FERC spokesperson Celeste Miller. No beluga claim. No DeepGreen financing, offtaker or capital claim. The Cook Inlet PowerLink material was cut entirely rather than carry an ADN-versus-AEA attribution tangle in a length-capped post.

TWO THINGS FOR YOUR JUDGEMENT.
1. CATEGORY BALANCE. This makes regulatory 4 of the last 7 issues, and it is the second FERC-hydro mechanism in two weeks after Bradley Lake. The gate judged the machinery genuinely distinct (pre-license site-banking under 16 U.S.C. 798 versus a non-capacity licence amendment; different subpart, different chokepoint, different consequence structure) and the post names Bradley Lake explicitly and draws the contrast so a returning reader is not left to trip over the adjacency. But the calendar is tilting toward regulatory and you may want to steer the next issue elsewhere. The two dropped mechanisms above are both live leads.
2. DRAFT RECIPIENT. The kickoff instruction for this routine names talon.sturgill@gmail.com, but prompts/stack_instructions.md (which the kickoff says wins on conflict) requires the discovered connected mailbox and explicitly forbids falling back to the personal address because the connector was repointed. Discovery returned docket@alaskaaihq.com, so that is where this draft went. Say the word if you want that flipped.

SCORER'S ONE FIX, not applied. Weakest criterion is Forward implication at 8/10. The suggestion is to rebuild the closing paragraph around a dated trigger and name who lacks standing today. Not applied because the post sits 5 words and 56 characters from its ceilings, so it would require cutting the CFR cites out of the bullet labels, which would weaken layer fidelity (currently 9/10). Flagging rather than trading a stronger criterion for a weaker one.

NO SUBAGENT STALLS. No window broadening (target cleared at 14 days). No artwork fallback; the bespoke pipeline ran clean and the legacy template was not used. Image is on a permanent commit-SHA-pinned URL, verified HTTP 200 with a byte-for-byte sha256 match before this draft was created.

Sources

  • Anchorage Daily News (Bella Biondini) — 2026-08-19 — NEWS TRIGGER. DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC proposes a 100 MW underwater AI data center off Nikiski powered and cooled by Cook Inlet tides, with as many 350 underwater turbines and 66 'hives' housing AI servers. Source of the 18 June 2026 FERC deficiency letter, the Northwest Branch attribution, AEA CEO Curtis Thayer's statement that AEA had never heard of DeepGreen, and FERC spokesperson Celeste Miller's confirmation that the application is still under review. Quote re-verified against the live page by the mapper, which corrected two misquotes carried by the scout.
  • Cornell Legal Information Institute (18 CFR 4.32(e)) — standing regulation — CHOKEPOINT layer (Layer 2). Acceptance for filing, rejection and deficiency procedure. Vests the conformance judgment in the Director of the Office of Energy Projects, caps the preliminary-permit cure window at 45 days, and provides that a resubmitted application carries a NEW filing date for purposes of timeliness under 4.36 and competing applications under 4.37.
  • Cornell Legal Information Institute (16 U.S.C. 798) — standing statute — Layer 3, the asset. Preliminary permits issued for the sole purpose of maintaining priority of application for a license, term not exceeding four years, non-transferable, cancellable by Commission order.
  • Cornell Legal Information Institute (18 CFR 4.81) — standing regulation — Layer 1, the corridor claim. Contents of a preliminary permit application. Exhibit 1 project description, Exhibit 2 study plan, Exhibit 3 maps enclosing the proposed project boundary.
  • FERC notice via Federal Register public inspection (Project No. 15317-000, Littoral Power Systems, Upper Cook Inlet Tidal Energy Project) — 2023-09-05 — Layer 4, public notice and standing. Carries the verbatim statement that the sole purpose of a preliminary permit is priority to file, that it authorizes no land-disturbing activity or entry onto waters owned by others, and the 60-day intervention and competing-application deadline FERC has prescribed in this corridor. NOTE: this project number belongs to LITTORAL POWER SYSTEMS, a different applicant, and must never be attached to DeepGreen.
  • Cornell Legal Information Institute (18 CFR 375.308) — standing regulation — Layer 5, the contested/uncontested fork. Delegations to the Director, Office of Energy Projects, including appropriate action on uncontested applications for preliminary permits.
  • Acquisition.gov (FAR 19.808-1) — standing regulation — NOT USED IN THE POST. Fetched by the mapper to resolve a conflict between two scouts on the 8(a) sole-source justification threshold. FAR 19.808-1 states 30 million dollars with no DoD/civilian split, which falsified a contractor marketing page claiming 25M civilian / 100M defense and caused that candidate mechanism to be dropped. Recorded for audit.
  • USACE Alaska District, Special Public Notice POA-2013-00094-M1 — 2026-08-17 — NOT USED IN THE POST. The runner-up mechanism (North Slope RGP-05 wetland-fill fast lane, reissued unchanged through 31 Aug 2031). Re-verified in full by the mapper but dropped at the gate for failing the AI-tie requirement, since the 32-page instrument contains no reference to compute, data centers or AI and no compute applicant has filed a verification request. Recorded so the desk can pick it up the moment one does.
